newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-USG gasoline diffs jump higher.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-USG gasoline diffs jump higher.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast gasoline differentials roared higher Monday on a pipeline scheduling deadline, grabbing attention away from what was relatively subdued activity in New York Harbor and the Midcontinent.
Apart from the scheduling deadline, there was little news on the cash products side following the long holiday weekend.
NYMEX crude oil futures, meanwhile, were down partly because of the sell-off late last week and talk Iraqi oil sales were nearing.

In the U.S. Gulf, prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline jumped more than 1.00 cent to trade as high as 0.50 cent under the August NYMEX, with the scheduling deadline for the front 20th cycle on the Colonial Pipeline looming at the end of the day.
M1 differentials have gained sharply on nearly every schedulng deadline on the Colonial, the main artery from the Gulf Coast to the East Coast, for the past two months.
Buying in the conventional barrels emerged from both traders and refiners, according to sources.
Reformulated A1 gasoline was talked at about 2.50 cents over the prompt M1 barrels, or about 2.00 cents over the August NYMEX.
"It's hard to get a good A1 number, especially with the way the M's keep jumping around," one trader said.
Distillate trade appeared more subdued, though prompt low sulphur diesel barrels were offered at about 1.60 cents under the August futures, up about 0.10 cent from last week.
Reformulated A2 gasoline differentials inched higher early Monday, with a prompt deal heard at 0.15 cent over the August futures, up about 0.20 cent from last week.
Prompt conventional M2 gasoline held onto its strength, hovering between about 2.25 and 2.50 cents under the August NYMEX, according to traders.

In Group Three, prompt conventional unleaded gasoline differentials continued to weaken after falling about a half cent last week amid ample supply. Differentials on Monday eased a quarter to a half cent, putting sellers at 2.00 cents over August NYMEX futures.
"It's still pretty quiet," said a trader, noting some players have not yet returned from the Fourth of July holiday weekend.

Any month unleaded differentials remained steady at 0.75/1.00 cents. Chicago prompt gasoline differentials also held at 1.75/2.00 cents but third cycle material edged up about a quarter 1.25/1.50 cents over the print.
On the distillate side, Group prompt low sulphur held steady but the any months dipped a quarter cent on perceptions of good supply.
